title: Acumen Pharmaceuticals Announces $35.75 Million Private Placement to Advance Potential Best-in-Class Molecules from Amyloid Beta Oligomer-Selective Enhanced Brain Delivery Portfolio
content:
Acumen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: ABOS) announced that it has entered into a securities purchase agreement with certain institutional and accredited investors for a private placement of approximately $35.75 million of shares of its common stock at a price of $3.30 per share.

The private placement was led by existing investor RA Capital Management, with participation from other investors, including ADAR1 Capital Management, Sands Capital, and a large investment management firm. The private placement is expected to close on or about March 16, 2026.

Proceeds from the financing are expected to primarily support Acumen's Enhanced Brain Delivery (EBD) program, including ongoing preclinical development work to support the nomination of a lead clinical candidate molecule, and for working capital and other general corporate purposes. Submission of an IND with respect to a lead clinical candidate is targeted for mid-2027.

EBD Non-Human Primate (NHP) Study Results: Acumen also announced certain preclinical data, including in vitro, in vivo and NHP study results, that support development candidates in Acumen's EBD program, conducted utilizing JCR Pharmaceuticals' blood-brain barrier penetrating technology, J-Brain Cargo®.

Enhanced Brain Penetration: Development candidates achieved 14-40x higher brain levels in NHPs compared to native antibodies at 24 hours. Low Anemia Risk: Hematology data in NHPs indicate low potential for anemia with no adverse effects observed. Subcutaneous Dosing Capability: Favorable stability profile and enhanced brain delivery support subcutaneous administration with low-volume devices.

Acumen's EBD program is part of an ongoing collaboration between Acumen and JCR announced in July 2025. J-Brain Cargo® technology is JCR's proprietary drug delivery system that efficiently delivers drugs to target tissues, including the central nervous system, through receptor-mediated transcytosis.

About Acumen Pharmaceuticals: Acumen is currently focused on advancing its lead investigational product candidate, sabirnetug (ACU193), a humanized monoclonal antibody that selectively targets toxic soluble AβOs, in its ongoing Phase 2 clinical trial ALTITUDE-AD (NCT06335173) in early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease patients, following positive results in its Phase 1 trial INTERCEPT-AD. Acumen is also investigating a subcutaneous formulation of sabirnetug using Halozyme's proprietary ENHANZE® drug delivery technology.

title: Anavex Life Sciences Provides Update on Regulatory Review in the EU for Blarcamesine to Treat Early Alzheimer's Disease
content:
Anavex Life Sciences Corp. announced that it has withdrawn its application for the marketing authorization of blarcamesine in the EU as an add-on therapy for the treatment of early Alzheimer's disease in adults, which had been under review by the European Medicines Agency (EMA).

The decision to withdraw the application follows feedback from the EMA's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) indicating that it would not be in a position to issue a positive opinion for the application at this time. The Company remains committed to the ongoing clinical development of blarcamesine and to advancing potential therapeutic options addressing the significant unmet medical needs of patients living with early Alzheimer's disease, also motivated by the strong support received by Alzheimer's disease patients and organizations, including Alzheimer Europe.

Anavex had submitted the application following encouragement by the SME Office of the EMA in October 2023 when the EMA representatives encouraged Anavex 'to immediately begin preparing' for the application and that the 'next step for Anavex in terms of interactions with EMA would be to apply for a marketing authorization application.' Anavex now has to take note of the differing assessment of the CHMP at the EMA and will consider the constructive feedback received from the CHMP and focus on gathering additional data and conducting further analyses to address the points raised by the CHMP.

About Blarcamesine (ANAVEX®2-73): Blarcamesine is an orally available drug candidate designed to restore cellular homeostasis by targeting SIGMAR1 and muscarinic receptors. Preclinical studies demonstrated its potential to halt and/or reverse the course of Alzheimer's disease. Blarcamesine also exhibited anticonvulsant, anti-amnesic, neuroprotective, and anti-depressant properties in animal models. Anavex's lead drug candidate has successfully completed a Phase 2a and a Phase 2b/3 clinical trial for Alzheimer's disease, a Phase 2 proof-of-concept study in Parkinson's disease dementia, and both a Phase 2 and a Phase 3 study in adult patients and one Phase 2/3 study in pediatric patients with Rett syndrome. The Company believes that ANAVEX®3-71, which targets SIGMAR1 and M1 muscarinic receptors, is a promising clinical stage drug candidate demonstrating disease-modifying activity against the major hallmarks of Alzheimer's disease in transgenic (3xTg-AD) mice, including cognitive deficits, amyloid, and tau pathologies.

title: CervoMed Announces New Data at the AD/PD™ 2026 Scientific Conference that Reinforce Neflamapimod's Positive Effects in Dementia with Lewy Bodies (DLB) in Patients without Alzheimer's Disease Co-Pathology
content:
New analyses of data from the RewinD-LB Phase 2b trial, stratified by plasma pTau181 level, demonstrate a progressively greater treatment effect with neflamapimod as patients are enriched for absence of Alzheimer's disease co-pathology.

The RewinD-LB Phase 2b trial was comprised of an initial, randomized phase comparing neflamapimod to placebo, followed by a neflamapimod-only extension phase. In the initial phase, participants did not achieve expected plasma drug concentration levels with DP Batch A capsules and did not demonstrate a statistically significant improvement on the trial's primary endpoint. In the extension phase, administration of DP Batch B was associated with expected plasma drug concentration levels and demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful slowing of clinical progression.

Within-participant comparison of change in CDR-SB over 16 weeks in those who received placebo and then DP Batch B, stratified by pTau181 level at screening:
- pTau181 <27.2 pg/mL (60-65% without AD co-pathology, n=32): CDR-SB difference -0.08, p=0.9
- pTau181 <25.2 pg/mL (70-75% without AD co-pathology, n=28): CDR-SB difference -0.55, p=0.044
- pTau181 <23 pg/mL (75-80% without AD co-pathology, n=24): CDR-SB difference -0.71, p=0.034
- pTau181 <21 pg/mL (80-90% without AD co-pathology, n=21): CDR-SB difference -1.11, p=0.005

Similarly, ADCS-CGIC score differences between DP Batch B and placebo: at <27.2 pg/mL the difference was -0.44 (p=0.044); at <21 pg/mL the difference was -0.82 (p=0.004). DP Batch A showed no effect across all four pTau181 subgroups.

New PK/PD analyses: The estimated threshold for therapeutic activity was a trough plasma drug concentration (Ctrough) of 4 ng/mL. DP Batch B achieved this threshold in 75% of participants vs. 50% for DP Batch A (p=0.02). Patients in the DP Batch A group who achieved Ctrough ≥4 ng/mL showed clinical effects similar to DP Batch B; those who did not were similar to placebo.

The <21.0 pg/mL cut-off level of plasma pTau181 will be used as an enrichment criterion in the Company's planned Phase 3 trial. At this cut-off, an estimated 80-90% of enrolled patients will be without AD co-pathology. CervoMed plans to initiate Phase 3 in H2 2026, subject to available funding.

title: NKGen Biotech Reports Combined Phase 1 Troculeucel Data Demonstrating Dose-Responsive Cognitive Improvements and Biomarker Correlations in Alzheimer's Disease at AD/PD 2026™
content:
NKGen Biotech reported combined Phase 1 analyses from two previously completed open-label Phase 1 trials of troculeucel in Alzheimer's disease (NCT04678453; NCT06189963) at AD/PD™ 2026.

Pooled analysis focusing on the moderate AD stage population demonstrated clear dose-responsive cognitive trends. Cognitive outcomes at 3-month assessment (n=6 moderate AD patients):
- 100% of patients were stable or improved across all established MCID thresholds: ADAS-Cog (±4 points), CDR-SB (±2 points), ADCOMS (±0.1 points)
- No cognitive decline was observed in any patient
- Higher doses (4–6B cells) were associated with greater directional improvement and more frequent MCID exceedance
- 50% of patients improved from the moderate to mild range on CDR-SB at three months

Durability: In the two patients remaining on therapy for 12 months, improvements across cognitive measures were maintained throughout treatment. Safety: Troculeucel was very well tolerated, with no treatment-related adverse events reported across both Phase 1 studies.

Plasma GFAP biomarker correlations:
- Baseline GFAP correlated with CDR-SB (r=0.60, p=0.044) and ADCOMS (r=0.64, p=0.030)
- After three months of therapy, GFAP continued to correlate with CDR-SB (r=0.57, p=0.056) and ADCOMS (r=0.66, p=0.022)
- In moderate AD patients receiving ≥4 billion cells (n=4): CDR-SB r=0.76 (p=0.009) and ADCOMS r=0.71 (p=0.018)
- Pooled longitudinal analyses: CDR-SB r=0.56 (p=0.001) and ADCOMS r=0.50 (p=0.004)

About Troculeucel: Troculeucel is a novel cell-based, patient-specific, ex vivo expanded autologous NK cell immunotherapeutic drug candidate. The ongoing Phase 2 trial for moderate stage Alzheimer's disease is actively enrolling. Results reported are from the completed Phase 1 trials and do not include results from the ongoing Phase 2 trial.

title: A Dual 6-Month & 18-Month Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind, Clinical Trial Investigating Efficacy and Safety of Buntanetap in Early Alzheimer's Participants
content:
AD/PD™ 2026 Abstract #3582. Poster on Board — β-Amyloid Diseases / Drug Development, Clinical Trials / New Clinical Trial Designs.

Aims: In a Phase 2b dose-ranging study in participants with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease (NCT05686044), buntanetap (also known as Posiphen) demonstrated a statistically significant cognitive improvement in plasma pTau217-positive participants with mild AD. These cognitive benefits were supported by biomarker findings showing that buntanetap reduced neurotoxic aggregation proteins, decreased inflammation, and improved neuronal function. To validate these effects, a new pivotal clinical trial in early AD was initiated in April 2025 (NCT06709014).

Methods: A prospective, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 3 study is currently ongoing. A total of 760 participants with early AD will be enrolled across 83 sites in the United States. This dual-study will include efficacy readout at both 6-month and 18-month, to evaluate buntanetap's symptomatic and disease-modifying treatment effects.

Results: Updates on site activation status, screening procedures, screen failure rates and key drivers, enrollment pace, and the projected timeline for database lock.

Conclusions: The Phase 3 study in early AD is ongoing. Key insights and lessons learned throughout the conduct of the trial were shared.

Background on buntanetap: Buntanetap is an oral translation inhibitor that reduces production of amyloid precursor protein (APP), alpha-synuclein, and tau by targeting iron-responsive elements in the 5'UTR of their mRNA. The Phase 2b study in mild-to-moderate AD (NCT05686044) showed statistically significant cognitive improvement in pTau217-positive mild AD patients, with supporting biomarker evidence of reduced neurotoxic aggregation proteins, decreased inflammation, and improved neuronal function.

title: ProMIS Neurosciences Announces Full Year 2025 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Highlights
content:
ProMIS Neurosciences reported that enrollment was completed in December 2025 in PRECISE-AD, its Phase 1b clinical trial of PMN310 in Alzheimer's disease, with 144 participants enrolled (vs. a target of 128) across 3 dosing cohorts (5, 10, 20 mg/kg IV). The trial was oversubscribed. PMN310 continues to demonstrate a generally favorable safety profile with no treatment-related Serious Adverse Events to date. The Data and Safety Monitoring Board recommended advancement to cohort 3 (the study's highest planned dose level) with no safety concerns identified.

PRECISE-AD (NCT06750432) is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics of multiple ascending doses of intravenous PMN310 in patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment due to AD or mild AD (Stage 3 and Stage 4 AD). The study is powered to provide 95% confidence for detection of ARIA and is designed to provide meaningful insight into the effects of PMN310 on biomarkers and clinical outcomes. PRECISE-AD will be the first study to examine the effects of a monoclonal antibody directed solely against Aβ oligomers on biomarkers associated with AD pathology.

Timeline: Six-month assessments expected to be completed in Q2 2026. Blinded interim analysis anticipated in early Q3 2026. Completion of all patient visits expected Q4 2026. Top-line data anticipated in early 2027 following database lock and statistical analysis.

About PMN310: PMN310 is a humanized IgG1 antibody directed toward toxic amyloid-beta oligomers (AβO) that avoids binding to amyloid plaque — a mechanism believed to be a primary driver of ARIA associated with other anti-amyloid antibodies. PMN310 was granted FDA Fast Track Designation in July 2025. ProMIS closed a $75.5 million private placement in February 2026, providing cash runway through 2027. The company has accelerated development of a subcutaneous formulation of PMN310.

EpiSelect™ platform: ProMIS's computational platform identifies conformational epitopes uniquely exposed on toxic misfolded proteins, enabling generation of misfolding-specific antibodies. This produced PMN310, which has been shown to be highly selective for toxic Aβ oligomers without significant reactivity with Aβ monomers or fibrils, thereby avoiding target distraction by these more abundant species and potentially reducing the risk of brain edema and microhemorrhages associated with targeting vascular/parenchymal amyloid.
